card.name: Subject nouns before reported-event verbs
card.fires_on: The last word of a subject noun phrase that is about to take a verb like "have been reported" or "occurred". It fires on words such as "cases" after postmarketing, a symptom name, or "patients".

modes.label: Postmarketing cases
modes.description: The word "cases" right after post-marketing in warning summaries.
modes.example: • Post-marketing<< cases>> of hepatosplenic T-cell lymph

modes.label: Symptom or finding names
modes.description: The end of an adverse-effect noun, often partway through the word, before "have been reported" or "occurred".
modes.example: Letharg<<y>> and somnolence have been reported

modes.label: Patients as subject
modes.description: The word "patients" or a verb after it in a news quote, before a statement about what they do.
modes.example: said his<< patients>> are increasingly concerned about the chemical.

card.writes: It favors adverbs and comment words such as "surprisingly" and "invariably" and suppresses hedges such as "perhaps" and "possibly".
card.plain: It marks the spot where a subject like "cases" or a symptom is complete and a statement about what was seen or reported comes next.
